name: Meu Dinheiro
tagline: Brazilian web app for tracking personal and family finances: accounts, categories, budgets, bills and reports.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible product is a ledger with categories, recurring bills, budget limits and a few charts, and an agent can produce that in an afternoon with SQLite and a chart library. What it cannot produce in one session is the boring plumbing that makes a finance app stick: automatic bank and card feeds, which in Brazil means Open Finance credentials or a paid aggregator, plus OFX quirks per bank. You can cover most of the gap with manual entry and OFX/CSV import, which is honestly how a lot of people use these tools anyway. The other gap is shape rather than code: a phone-friendly interface you will actually open at the checkout counter, and a spouse who can log in too. Build it if you like owning your numbers, keep paying if the appeal was the bank sync doing the typing for you.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you record income and expenses against accounts and categories, import OFX/CSV statements from your bank, set monthly budget limits, and see where the money went.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine or small VPS to run it on
OFX or CSV statement exports from your bank for anything you do not want to type
Willingness to categorize transactions yourself for the first few weeks
whatYouLose: Automatic bank and credit card synchronization via Open Finance or an aggregator
A polished mobile experience for logging spend on the spot
Multi-user family access with sane permissions
Someone else's category taxonomy and reports that already match how Brazilian household bills work
Backups, uptime and recovery when your laptop dies mid-month
moatNotes: The moat is not the ledger, it is the pipe into the bank. Open Finance access is credentialed and regulated, so a hobby build either pays an aggregator or imports files by hand.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the hard part of personal finance software is not arithmetic, it is getting transactions into the system without you noticing. A paid product that pulls statements from your bank and card issuer, guesses categories, and nags you on your phone will beat a lovely self-hosted ledger that requires a monthly file-import ritual, because the ledger you stop updating is worth zero. Add a shared family login and a vendor that keeps the data alive across a laptop replacement, and the subscription is cheap relative to the chance you abandon the habit.
notes: Double entry purists will reach for Beancount or Actual Budget instead, and they are not wrong.
prompt:
Build a single-user personal finance tracker that runs locally. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable:
- Next.js (App Router) with TypeScript and Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/financas.db, schema created on first run
- Recharts for charts
- Locale pt-BR, currency BRL, dates dd/MM/yyyy

Data model:
- accounts: id, name, type (conta_corrente | poupanca | cartao_credito | dinheiro | investimento), opening_balance
- categories: id, name, kind (receita | despesa), parent_id nullable
- transactions: id, account_id, category_id, date, amount (integer centavos, signed), description, notes, tags, import_hash nullable unique
- budgets: id, category_id, month (YYYY-MM), limit_cents
- recurring: id, description, account_id, category_id, amount_cents, day_of_month, active

Features, in scope:
- Transaction list with filters by date range, account, category and free text search; inline edit and delete
- Quick-add form that remembers the last used account and category
- Import OFX and CSV statements: file upload, column/field mapping for CSV, dedupe via import_hash built from date + amount + description, a review screen where each imported row gets a category before commit
- Category rules: if a description matches a stored substring, auto-assign a category on import
- Dashboard: current balance per account, month income vs expense, expenses by category (pie), 12 month trend (bar), budget progress bars with over-limit in red
- Recurring bills page that generates the current month's pending entries with one click
- Monthly report page, printable, plus CSV export of all transactions
- Seed script with a realistic pt-BR category tree (moradia, alimentacao, transporte, saude, educacao, lazer, salario, etc)

Out of scope, do not attempt:
- Open Finance or any bank API integration, no scraping bank sites
- Multi-user, auth, sharing, mobile apps, double entry accounting, invoices or tax reports

Rules:
- Store money as integer centavos everywhere, format only at render time
- Any config in .env with a .env.example committed, never hardcode paths or secrets
- Include a npm run backup script that copies the SQLite file with a timestamp
- README with setup, import instructions and a one paragraph note on what this deliberately does not do
- Ship it working: npm install, npm run seed, npm run dev
